Europe PMC search API, resultType=core, pageSize=20; first 20 records screened for each listed query (or all when fewer). Missing common-name, chemical, rhythm and eye queries were sent here after OpenAlex HTTP 429, on coordinator instruction.
General web search for the listed supplemental common-name, chemical, rhythm, eye and family-review queries; excluded Wikipedia/ResearchGate/encyclopedia results without opening them.
Harvest titles and stored abstracts screened; direct Europe PMC abstracts retrieved for 52 harvested DOI records. Harvest citations of 10.3389/fpls.2015.00207 and 10.1016/j.tree.2009.09.010 screened.

Full text opened: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC59234/ (root-hair chemical response); Europe PMC fullTextXML PMC10934225 (blue-light gene-expression response); PMC7353751 (PHYA), PMC9203126 (shade/flowering), PMC11720064 (light-quality treatments), PMC10610208 (M. lupulina mycorrhizal transcriptome), PMC12278555 (M. lupulina PAT1), PMC13661613 (M. truncatula interplant signals), PMC12058308 (alfalfa review), PMC13577728 (Fabaceae flowering review), PMC10724382 (plant-vision model).

The M. lupulina PAT1 study tested wound/grafting responses and heterologous tobacco localization/transactivation, not a measured light-sensing response in M. lupulina. Mycorrhizal transcriptomic GO labels were not treated as receptor measurements. The compound-eye plant model is a theoretical analogy, with no measured eye in Medicago.
Direct abstract pages read: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1132536/ and https://europepmc.org/article/MED/30924988. Corresponding evidence is partial.

Canon: in-hand compilation evidence checked for Medicago. Animal Eyes 2nd edition has no Medicago entry in the logged evidence; no plant sense_chemical or sense_light_nonvisual canon compilation is in hand. Canon completion remains governed by THOROUGH.md.

Access limits: api.openalex.org HTTP 429, portlandpress.com and onlinelibrary.wiley.com HTTP 403; stopped each provider and notified coordinator. PMC PDF and one later article request served robot-challenge HTML (HTTP 200), not paper text. No challenge was bypassed.
note: Null result applies to the remaining queued species listed in for. M. sativa light and chemical responses were found and logged separately in harvest-c1; M. truncatula has existing evidence and was not included in the null scope. No carry rule transfers these plant sense measurements to the other species. All results, including the Fabaceae review, were checked for those remaining species; no corresponding direct measurement was found. This is not a claim that the genus lacks light/chemical sensing.
